blocks.etymology: From Middle English witty, witti, from Old English wittiġ, witiġ, ġewittiġ (“clever, wise”), from Proto-West Germanic *witīg, *witag, from Proto-Germanic *witagaz, *wītagaz (“knowing, wise, clever”), equivalent to wit + -y. Cognate with Middle Low German wittich, gewittich (“knowing, clever, wise, understanding”), German witzig (“funny, witty”), Norwegian Bokmål vettig, Norwegian Nynorsk vittig (“witty”).

senses.definition: Able to say clever and funny things quickly.

examples.en: Everyone laughed at her witty remarks during dinner.
examples.vi: Mọi người đều bật cười trước những nhận xét dí dỏm của cô ấy trong bữa tối.

senses.vi: dí dỏm; hóm hỉnh

vi_block: Dí dỏm, hóm hỉ, tế nhị.

examples: His speech was both witty and informative.
wiktionary.gloss: Clever; amusingly ingenious.

examples: His frequent quips mark him as particularly witty.
wiktionary.gloss: Full of wit.

examples: She may have grown older, but she has grown no less witty.
wiktionary.gloss: Quick of mind; insightful; in possession of wits.

tatoeba.en: They aren't as witty as they used to be.
tatoeba.vi: Họ không còn dí dỏm như trước kia nữa.
